body:
You are drafting short lines of game text for a single-player D&D 2024 computer RPG set in Curse of Strahd's Barovia. Reply in plain text only. Do not message, route to, or ask anyone else; finish with your reply.

HOUSE RULES FOR ALL LINES
- ALLUDE, NEVER QUOTE. This game winks at another famous fantasy game in small ways, but no line may contain a name, quote, or catchphrase from another game, and no line may mention a game, a player, dice, rolls, levels or saving. Everything happens inside the world.
- The tone is gothic, dry and quietly funny, never cruel. The joke is in what is there.
- Give TWO options for every line so the editor can choose. Label each option A or B.
- Spoken lines are formatted: Speaker [mood]: Text   (mood optional: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary). One or two sentences a line.
THE NARRATOR (voice rules): an old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather: interested, no illusions. Second person, present tense ("You crouch..."), or the acting hero as {name}. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn. Concrete senses, not adjectives. Never tells the player what to feel. No modern slang. When an animal speaks through the Speak with Animals spell, the Narrator reports it in quotes, in plain animal pictures (a dog says "the digger-man", "the box-maker").
CAMP TALKS: the party camps at night; a companion asks for a word. Companion lines are written "Name: text" (their own voice). The player picks short replies (write each as "> reply text") and each reply gets one or two lines of answer. Keep every line one or two sentences.

PARTY BANTER plays while the party walks: two companions talk, 3 to 5 lines in all, one or two sentences each, format "Name: text".
ILSE: human fighter, ex-soldier: short declarative sentences, military rhythm; counts things out loud; "Noted." "Hold." "Not my first funeral." "Count off."
WREN: halfling monk, ex-entertainer: fast, wry, London; "Easy." "Rude." "I'll allow it."
GODRICK: goliath paladin, big, warm, hearty, sincere; simple words and plans; takes figures of speech literally; "Right then!" "Fear not." "Sir Pellam always said..." Real: "Right. Big door. Spooky. I'll go first, I'm the largest."
LIRIEL: high elf cleric of the dawn god: soft, clear, musical, formal, gentle; "Morning's grace." "Be at peace." Speaks of her god as a close friend: "He's laughing at me, I think."
THISTLE: loud, blunt, rough grammar; "Grandda says...", "Bark and bones!", "Again!" Loves arm-wrestling Godrick (she always wins).

BANTER 1 (Ilse and Wren), after a fight in which someone threw a chair, a stool or a crate at a foe: is throwing the furniture a technique? Ilse disapproves on principle and then counts how well it worked; Wren is delighted.
BANTER 2 (Godrick and Liriel), same trigger: Godrick is proud of the chair; Liriel blesses it.
BANTER 3 (Godrick and Thistle): Godrick tells Thistle about the strongest arm-wrestler he ever met, before this valley: a horned woman with a laugh like a forge, whose heart ran so hot he had to wear an iron gauntlet to take her hand; she cried afterwards because she couldn't hug anyone; he still has the scorched gauntlet. Thistle wants to meet her, and to win. Warm, a little sad.
THE DREAM (Narrator, after a night at the Amber Temple, a temple of dark powers in amber, after the party has accepted a dark gift there): no joke at all. You dream of a stranger wearing the face of the person you would most like to see again, on the deck of a ship that is not there, who promises to keep the new darkness in you quiet, if only you will use it. One or two sentences, under 45 words.

Return in this layout (A/B for each):
B1-A: Ilse: ... | Wren: ... | Ilse: ... | Wren: ...
B1-B: Ilse: ... | Wren: ... | Ilse: ... | Wren: ...
B2-A: Godrick: ... | Liriel: ... | Godrick: ...
B2-B: Godrick: ... | Liriel: ... | Godrick: ...
B3-A: Godrick: ... | Thistle: ... | Godrick: ... | Thistle: ...
B3-B: Godrick: ... | Thistle: ... | Godrick: ... | Thistle: ...
DREAM-A: Narrator: ...
DREAM-B: Narrator: ...
result:
B1-A: Ilse: Throwing the furniture is not standard infantry doctrine. | Wren: Easy, sergeant, the stool had lovely form in the air. | Ilse: One shattered leg, two cracked ribs, one downed ghoul. Noted. | Wren: See? I'll allow it.
B1-B: Ilse: Hold. A tavern chair is not an issued weapon. | Wren: Bit rude to tell the chair that after all its hard work. | Ilse: Twelve paces, square impact, target neutralized on the first bounce. | Wren: Proper monastic discipline, that was.
B2-A: Godrick: Right then! That oak stool fought with the heart of a squire. | Liriel: Morning's grace upon its splinters, though I think my lord is laughing at us both. | Godrick: Fear not, I shall carry its stoutest leg in memoriam.
B2-B: Godrick: Sir Pellam always said a true defender uses whatever stands at hand, even the dining room. | Liriel: Be at peace, brave little crate; you have served the dawn well today. | Godrick: Right, if we find a matching table, the shadows haven't a chance.
B3-A: Godrick: Best arm-wrestler I ever met before this mist was a horned woman with a laugh like a roaring forge, whose heart burned so hot I had to wear an iron gauntlet just to clasp her hand. She wept after she pinned me, poor soul, because she couldn't hug a friend without scorching them, and I still keep that blackened gauntlet in my pack. | Thistle: Bark and bones, a woman made of fire! When we get out of this valley, you take me straight to her and I'll pin her in two! | Godrick: Right then, we will just need to find you a very thick pair of mittens first. | Thistle: Grandda says burnt knuckles just mean you held on proper!
B3-B: Godrick: You remind me of a horned warrior I wrestled once, who laughed like a smithy bellows and burned so fiercely inside that she charred my iron gauntlet right through the leather lining. She beat me fair, then cried into her ale because she hadn't been able to embrace a living soul in ten years, though I still carry that scorched glove for luck. | Thistle: Bark and bones, nobody cries at my table! Point me at her when the fog clears, Godrick—I'll give her a proper match and a bear-hug right after, blisters and all! | Godrick: Fear not, little friend, between the two of us we could weather a furnace. | Thistle: Right! Now set your elbow on that rock—again!
DREAM-A: Narrator: Salt wind that smells of nothing stirs the rigging of a ship with no hull beneath your boots, and the stranger wearing the face you miss most lays a warm hand over the amber cold in your chest. They promise the new hunger inside you will sleep like a hound, if only you let it off the chain when they ask.
DREAM-B: Narrator: You stand on a phantom deck above a sea of dry mist while someone wearing the one face you prayed never to see in this valley steps close enough to share their breath. They whisper that the dark thing coiled behind your ribs will never speak a word against you, so long as you feed it to get home.
